newsitem.title: USA: Allied Irish may shed branches in U.S deal.
newsitem.headline: Allied Irish may shed branches in U.S deal.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc, which has a deal pending to acquire Pennsylvania-based Dauphin Deposit Corp, would divest some branches in York County, Pa., if necessary to win regulatory approval for the deal, Jeremiah Casey, chief executive USA, told analysts Thursday.
"We've looked at the possiblity," Casey said, adding that if there were any trimming of branches "it would be small."
Allied Irish has owned Baltimore-Based First Maryland Bancorp since 1989.
Casey, who is also chairman of First Maryland, said the two banks together would have about a 36 percent share in York County. He said concentrations above 30 percent often bring regulatory scrutiny.

"From a geograpahic point of view this is a great fit," Casey said of the planned combination. Combining the two banks, which serve contiguous areas, would give Allied Irish's U.S. unit a dominant market share in a corridor stretching from Harrisburg, Pa., to Baltimore.

Asked about the future role of Dauphin's Hopper Soliday & Co securities unit, which makes Dauphin one of only a small number of U.S. banks with approval to engage in securities underwriting, Casey said Allied Irish will look at the opportunities but is not attaching any special significance to it. He noted that Hopper Soliday has not traditionally done much equity underwriting.
In response to a question, Casey said there would be some job losses after the merger as a result of duplicative administrative and headquarters functions. He did not provide any figures.
The merger, worth about $1.36 billion, is expected to close early in the third quarter of 1997.
Allied Irish ADRs were up 1/8 to 44-1/8 Thursday afternoon. Dauphin Deposit shares were up 9/64 to 42-25/64.
